get.description:
Where this network can actually operate — one entry per country with a daughter company behind it.

Public on purpose, and the counterpart of the open-data rates: a shop deciding whether to sign up, a
store wondering whether we reach its customers, and (soon) a vendor integrating the shipping API all
ask the same question first — and the sign-up wizard needs it before anyone can choose. It is derived
from the sisters rather than listed, so a country cannot appear here that nobody could lawfully
invoice in. Structural only: which country, what it is called, what it settles in. The entity's own id
is the shape of the business and stays behind GET /entities, which is operator-only.

The rate book every cross-border price stands on: one rate per currency against the base, with when
it was taken and who from. Operator-only — not because it is a secret, but because a rate with no
context invites being read as a promise; what a customer sees is the rate ON THEIR QUOTE.

post.description:
Push a rate. This is the door a live feed comes through — the same one an operator uses by hand when
the feed is down, which is deliberate: there is one way a rate enters the system, and it is recorded
with its source either way.

get.description:
A sister's books: the trial balance, whether it balances, and the coverage read — money held against
money owed. Operator-only, and the closest thing the network has to an answer for "are we solvent",
which could not even be ASKED before the postings existed.

post.description: Hand a raised payout to the rail. Still not a payment — an attempt, with a reference.

The rail says it landed — the one call that moves money in the books.

Operator-gated because in the sandbox a person presses it. In a live deployment this is what the
provider's callback drives, and the door is deliberately the same one: nothing above here is allowed
to learn that a payment can complete merely because we asked for it.
It did not go. The payable stands, because the money is still owed.
It went and came back. Its own entry, never an unwinding of the first.

get.description: A sister's payouts, newest first — the settlement page.

post.description:
Turn a sister's margin knob. Operator-gated today because there is no per-sister admin role yet —
when there is, this is the endpoint it owns, scoped to its own entity and nobody else's.

It reprices nothing already quoted: every parcel carries the rate it was minted at.

Turn a sister's rate knobs — cost of risk, profit on risk, margin — for one lane of work or for
everything it does.

Three layers rather than one number because they answer different questions, and blended they answer
none: a sister earning well cannot otherwise tell whether the market is good or whether it is carrying
risk nobody is paying for. They ADD, they do not compound, and their sum is bounded so three
innocent-looking numbers cannot price a market out of existence.

Operator-gated for now, like the knob above. When sisters get their own administration this is one of
the endpoints it owns — scoped to its own entity — and a group-level console reads them side by side.

get.description:
What this sister actually charges for a lane of work, with the three layers stated. Operator-only:
 the split is for running the business, never for a customer.

post.description:
Set the tax a sister collects — a different kind of knob from the three above, and the one place in
this system where a rate is not ours to choose.

Two things it refuses. A rate above zero without a registration number: charging tax you are not
registered to collect is money taken from a customer in the name of an authority that has never heard
of you. And the group: it is the merchant of record nowhere, so it collects nothing anywhere.

Like every other rate here it reprices nothing already sold — a shipment carries the tax rate it was
minted at, because a rate change has a date and every sale before it was correctly taxed at the old one.

get.description:
The tax that applies to a lane of work, and the registration it is collected under. Operator-gated
 like its neighbours, though unlike the rate split this is not a secret: what a customer was charged
 and by whom appears on their own receipt.

post.description:
Set what a sister covers when it breaks something, and what it charges to cover more.

This is the policy an upheld damage award is checked against. Until it existed the network's
liability was undefined — an adjudicator had a number to type and nothing to check it against — and
a sanity bound in a service method was standing in for a commercial decision.

Every sister starts covering nothing, because a free limit invented in this codebase would be a
promise nobody costed. Setting one is a deliberate commercial act, exactly like the rates and the tax.

get.description:
What this sister covers on a lane of work. Not a secret — a shipper cannot decide whether to declare
 a value without knowing what is already covered and what more would cost, so the same figures ride
 on every public quote.

What a margin change actually did. Not just what each rate earned — that half is arithmetic — but
what happened to the NUMBER of shipments after it, which can only be observed. Read as a timeline of
spells, so a rate raised and then lowered again shows as two separate periods to compare.
Operator KYC review queue — agents awaiting a decision.

post.description: Weekly driver settlement (Finance · DRIVER_PAYOUT) — operator only.

F2 — the counter books a too-big (dedicated, P4+) walk-up as FREIGHT instead of refusing it (the perishable
 "book immediate or planned" + rural "the shop IS the PUDO" path). The acting agent is pinned to its token
 (operator may override) and is the on-platform originator; the customer pays a CASH budget cap at the counter
 (→ the freight's maxSpend ceiling, so no driver can claim above it) and settles OFF-PLATFORM — no shipperDid,
 so the load stays 'unpaid' and the agent's parcel-sized wallet is never billed a truck haul (the driver is
 still paid on delivery by the platform, as for any bulletin freight). Immediate or planned (F1). Returns a
 tracking code the agent prints for a phone-less customer.

get.description:
The operational parcel list (agent + hub screens). PG2: PROJECTED for everyone but an operator —
the raw record carries phones, hashes and the handover secrets (collection code / OTP), none of
which a list surface needs; before this, ANY valid token could read them all.

`status` takes a COMMA-SEPARATED list. A shop counter has two piles — what is waiting to go on a bus
and what a customer is coming to collect — and a single-status query made the second pile impossible
to ask for in one breath. The alternative, omitting the filter, returns every parcel the shop has ever
handled: unbounded, and growing, on the cheapest phone in the network.
The planned route for a parcel (origin PUDO → MDP(s) → dest PUDO), once a destination is known.

DT — the printable label for a parcel (reprint). The label no longer carries any release secret (it
 prints the public tracking key and the creation date), but reprinting someone's parcel label is still
 a support action rather than a public one, so it stays operator-only.

post.description: Reverse logistics: cancel a not-yet-delivered parcel (Created / At_PUDO / At_MDP) — operator only.
Destination PUDO receives a whole bag → shelves each parcel + frees the tote (closes the tote leg).

Merchant console sign-in (S15): store ID + the signing secret (issued once, at
registration) → a genesis-role actor token bound to the vendor's DID.  for the
same reason auth/login is: a caller cannot hold an actor token before signing in.

get.description:
Load a single vendor (so the merchant console can sign back into an existing store via ?vendor=).
Returns the public view — the signing secret is issued once at registration and never re-exposed.

patch.description:
Update the store profile: map pin (origin-PUDO ranking), address, callback URL, split policy.
 Owner-scoped (PG0): the callback URL + split policy are the store's webhook/money config — an
 unlabelled write would let ANY token redirect another store's callbacks or rewrite its pricing.

delete.description: Stop collecting here. Bags already claimed stay with the drivers who claimed them.

get.description: This store's keys, in a shape safe to render — never a secret, not even to its owner.

delete.description: Stop a key working. Kept rather than deleted, so "what was that key doing" stays answerable.

get.description: What this dock should be bagging: paid parcels grouped by destination, plus the bags already open.

post.description: Close the bag: the store's commitment, and the moment drivers near the dock are told it is ready.

get.description:
A vendor's shipment register (R0): their OWN inbound parcels, server-side searched / filtered /
 sorted / paginated. Returns { items, total } so the console can page. Owner-scoped (403 for non-owners).

Export the WHOLE matching set (every page, current filters) as CSV — the vendor's OWN shipment export.
 Owner-scoped. Declared before the :parcelId route so "export" is not captured as a parcel id.

Store-wide shipment counts (total / unpaid / active) for the console header — computed over the WHOLE
 store, never the current register page, so the "top up" nudge stays honest under any filter. Owner-scoped.
 Declared before the :parcelId route so "stats" is not captured as a parcel id.

Full detail for one order (the watch-only status screen's drill-down). Owner-scoped; strips the
 control-tower-only short-ship marker before it reaches the external merchant.

The buyer's checkout selections waiting to be shipped (the console's incoming-orders inbox). Owner-scoped:
 these carry buyer email/mobile, so only the store itself (or an operator) may read them.

post.description:
The embedded PUDO-picker node (or a webhook, or manual entry): capture the buyer's destination-PUDO
choice + email so it can pre-fill a shipment in the console. This is what hooks into the vendor's checkout.

get.description:
Vendor status-callback outbox (HMAC-signed ready_for_pickup / collected / disputed). Owner-scoped —
 the outbox holds signatures + payloads for this store only.

post.description:
Yes: mint the journey home, bill this store the figure the offer showed, and hand the shop its
 shelf slot back — which is the whole reason any of this exists.
No. The parcel stays exactly where it is, because it is still somebody else's property.

Derive the size tier from dimensions (cm) + weight (kg) — live preview for the mint form. S32c also
 returns the cargo class + whether it needs dedicated freight, so the mint form can warn BEFORE minting
 that a P4+ load won't ride the parcel network (it will be diverted to the dedicated-freight lane).
  (PG3): a pure derivation over the open size/cargo thresholds — no data is read, nothing is
 written. The anonymous Send wizard needs it: dims+weight are the ONLY size input now (no self-declared
 tiers), and a guest pricing a parcel must derive the tier before the (equally public) quote.

get.description:
Quote a shipment from the open-data participant rates: flexible (any carrier) vs locked (cheapest).
  (S13): the quote is derived ONLY from open-data prices — it is the SEE of See-Buy-Get,
 and a consumer holds no account to authenticate with.

Quote many candidates at once so each PUDO pin on the map carries a real total. Either fix the origin
and vary the destinations (buyer's map) or fix the destination and vary the origins (vendor's drop-off map).

Competitive price discovery, BOUNDED so it scales to 30k PUDOs. Returns a local **benchmark**
(median / p25–p75 / min–max / count of nearby same-type rates) + a **capped** set of nearby price
pins for the map — never the whole network. With `type` → that one service (PUDO/MDP per-parcel,
vehicle per-km); without `type` → just the three network benchmarks (the public hub summary).
Without lat/lng → network-wide (no radius filter). In-memory haversine here; a geo-index at real scale.
Open pricing feed — every PUDO, MDP and vehicle's advertised rate. DEBUG/small-network only — at scale use /pricing/near.

patch.description: A PUDO agent sets its open-data per-parcel handling price.
An MDP sets its open-data per-parcel sort price.
A driver / fleet manager sets a vehicle's open-data per-km transport rate.

Vendor prepays its balance with the per-country daughter company. Owner-scoped (PG0): money movement
 on a store's book is the store's own action, even in the crediting direction.

get.description:
A vendor's prepaid balance + settlement book (top-ups / billings / rebates). Owner-scoped — this is the
 store's money history. The searchable/paginated register is at .../ledger; this stays for the balance.

The vendor's bookkeeping register (R3): their OWN ledger, server-side searched / filtered / sorted /
 paginated → { items, total }. Owner-scoped (403 for non-owners).

Running totals (in / out / net / count) for the CURRENT filtered view, plus the always-current balance.
 Owner-scoped. Declared before no :sub route, but kept explicit for parity with the shipment register.

Export the WHOLE matching set (every page, current filters) as CSV — the vendor's OWN bookkeeping export.
 Owner-scoped.

post.description:
Retry the prepaid gate on an unpaid shipment after a top-up → issue the label + ParcelPaid.
 Owner-scoped (PG0): settling BILLS the minting store's balance, so only that store (or an
 operator) may trigger it — a storeless walk-up parcel has no settle path at all.

get.description:
Public track-and-trace by the shareable tracking key (no PII, no handover code).
  (S13): the comment above was always the intent — the KEY is the credential; the
 response carries no PII and no collection code, and the GET of See-Buy-Get cannot ask a
 consumer for an account it has no way to hold.

Resolve a free-text place/area/landmark to a point — the agent's "Address" intake mode geocodes a
typed area, then ranks the network points nearest-first client-side.  for the same open-data
reasoning as /quote + /network/points: a pure offline gazetteer lookup, no data read or written.
`confidence` (exact | approx | fallback) lets the UI flag an approximate pin.

The public network directory — the sanitized slice of the agent register a SENDER needs to
choose a drop-off or delivery point: name, zone, pin, open state, the open-data handling
price, rating and free shelf slots. NOTHING operational leaves here: no balance, no device,
no vault refs, no requirements — that is what keeps this  while GET /agents stays
token-gated (S3).

post.description:
Vendor mint: an order ships → create the inbound parcel + phygital label + collection code + tracking key.
 Owner-scoped (PG0): the mint BILLS dto.vendorId's prepaid balance, and vendorId comes from the BODY —
 without the gate any valid token could mint against (and drain) another store's book.

get.description:
PG2 — what the counter must know about a scanned parcel BEFORE confirming intake: what it is, what
 cash is due, where it goes. Field-picked (no phones, no handover secrets) and pinned to the acting
 shop — the same WRONG_PUDO rule the intake itself enforces, so the answer doubles as "is this mine
 to take in".

post.description: Destination PUDO shelves an arrived parcel → Ready_For_Pickup + buyer notified.
Buyer presents the collection QR → resolve the parcel + shelf slot (opens the handover screen).
Buyer confirms the parcel is correct → Delivered, order closed.

Control tower: rotate a parcel's burned release secret so a locked-out customer can still collect.
Operator-only — this is the recovery authority behind every "ask the control tower to reissue".
The new inbound collection code is never returned here; it reaches the buyer's app + the vendor.

get.description:
Control tower: the parcels whose owners gave up their claim and that nobody is paying to recover.

A QUEUE rather than a status, because what happens to them is decided by the law of the sister's
jurisdiction rather than by this system. Modelling a disposal rule we do not know would be worse
than showing an operator the list and letting them apply the one they do.

post.description:
Control tower: close out one of them, and settle what the shop is owed for having held it.

The only path on which the NETWORK absorbs the holding fee. Everywhere else it is recovered from
whoever ended the situation; here nobody did, and the alternative is a shortfall settling quietly on
a shopkeeper who did the work and had no say in any of it.
Buyer reports a discrepancy at collection → Disputed, with mandatory photo proof.
Tier-1 customer rates a delivered parcel → writes the agent composite to the shared core (graduation).

REP2 — an AGENT rates a DRIVER on the movement leg (pickup punctuality, on-time / after-hours arrival,
overnight holds, care, equipment). The acting agent is pinned to its token (operator may override). Gated
on a REAL interaction: the agent must have handed to / received from this driver (a badge is not secret, so
"knowing it" is not enough). One rating per agent↔driver pair, last-wins.

get.description:
REP1 — a provider's PUBLIC reputation profile: a PII-free trust surface (name, zone, pin, the aggregate
stars + count, a "new" flag below the min-ratings floor, and serving-since).  for the same
open-data reasoning as /network/points — nothing operational (no balance, device, vault refs or PII)
leaves here, and the agent's did + shop name + zone + pin are already public there. Agents only for now;
drivers/fleet/MDP get profiles in later reputation slices (this 404s a non-agent did until then).

The disputes waiting on a decision, oldest first — the case somebody has waited longest for is the
one that most needs an answer.

Everything an adjudicator needs is on the parcel already: the merchant's photo of the contents at
mint, the drop-off photo, the delivery photo, and the claimant's photo of the problem, all held on
a dispute-evidence clock so none of it is swept while the case is open.

post.description:
Decide one. Upheld, partly upheld, or rejected — and every one of them carries a note, because a
person whose goods arrived broken is owed an explanation even when they are not owed money.

An upheld award is paid to whoever CONTRACTED with the sister: the store for a merchant order, or a
recorded off-platform payable for a walk-up sender who paid cash and has no account here.

get.description: PUDO coverage heatmap — points + density + open/closed counts (feeds journey-leg planning).

post.description: Plan the journey: commit a first-mile node (given or assigned) and compute the legs + ETA.

get.description: Network revenue / float / ledger — operator only. A field token must never read this.

post.description: Force a recompute of the whole-map pulse now (it also recomputes on a 2-min timer).
Set an operator surge override for a zone — a cell key, or a lat/lng the server buckets into one.

delete.description: Lift an operator surge override from a zone.

post.description: Register a fresh laminated tote (QR + human code) into the pool at this MDP.

get.description: Totes currently at a location (MDP id or agent did).

post.description: Link a free bag to a single next destination so it can start taking parcels.
Drop a parcel into a bag (capacity-checked) — connects bag ↔ parcel.
Scan the bag onto a bus — one scan moves the whole tote + every parcel to On_Bus.
A bus drops a bag at an MDP → scan the bag code, empty it; parcels become unsorted (At_MDP).
Sort a parcel at an MDP → returns its next destination + the bag code to drop it in.

get.description:
The fleets on the network. Scoped, because the raw record carries the console credential.

Left unrestricted, this returned every fleet's `loginCode` to any authenticated caller — and the
login code is the whole of the fleet console's authentication, so reading this list was signing in
as anybody. An operator sees everything; a fleet sees itself; everyone else gets the name and status
and nothing that could be used against the company.

post.description:
Fleet console, step one: WHICH FLEET. Names the company, and hands back nothing else.

The code used to be the whole sign-in. One shared secret per company is a poor fit for a company
running twenty managers across as many depots: no record of who did what, no way to cut off one
leaver without re-issuing to everybody, and a code that is permanent access to whoever once saw it.
It selects the tenant now; the person proves who they are in step two.

Fleet console, step two: WHICH PERSON — and the only step that mints anything.

Checked against the identity spine, which already counts wrong PINs and locks out; the fleet code
never had either. The person must actually hold a fleet_manager role for THIS company, so knowing a
company code and holding some unrelated account is not a way in.

The token still carries the manager DID as both did and tenant, so every fleet-scoped read behaves
exactly as before. Recording WHICH PERSON acted needs a claim the actor token does not have yet —
the response names them so the console can say who is signed in, and the audit trail does not.

get.description: Managers awaiting a KYC decision (the GLOS operator review queue).

post.description: Upload business KYC (registration cert, operator licence, owner ID, proof of address) → KYC_PENDING.
GLOS operator vetting of a fleet manager — a manager/driver token must never self-approve.

Record the refundable operating bond → ACTIVE — operator only (the fleet console recorded its
own bond before S3: a self-approval loop wired into shipped UI).

get.description: A fleet manager sees only their own vehicles (actor.tenant); operator sees all.
The truck sub-type catalog (label + capacity + handling capabilities) for registration UIs.

post.description: Upload / update registration docs — re-evaluates the verified (dispatch-priority) flag.

get.description: A fleet manager sees only their own drivers (actor.tenant); operator sees all.

post.description: Heavy registry: upload ID + licence copy → KYC_PENDING.
Driver starts a shift by scanning the vehicle's dashboard QR → couples them for the day.

get.description: The vehicles this driver has driven before — the "which one today?" list, before they reach the yard.

post.description:
Say (or re-say) where this shift is going. Re-declaring mid-shift is the normal case: a driver who has
reached Addis turns round, and the loads worth telling them about are now the ones on the road back.

Switch off (or back on) the road we worked out from a load the driver took.

A switch rather than a question. Taking a load already said where they are going, so asking again — in
a vehicle, at the moment they are least able to answer — would spend an interruption on something we
already know. This is the way back for the driver who was only doing that one bag as a favour.

get.description: The roads this driver has run before — offered instead of making them name two places every morning.

post.description:
Declare a PATCH instead of a road: "I take work within this many km of me". For a bike or a bajaj there
is no corridor to name — there is a district, and it moves with them.

Hold new offers for a while — lunch, a fare of their own, a puncture, the last hour of a long day.
Stops NEW work only: whatever they are already carrying is still theirs to hand over and deliver.
Take work again, now.
Find work AROUND me rather than along a road — the same marketplace, matched by distance.
Driver closes the shift → decouples driver + vehicle.

"Do not wake me for less than this", all in, for both bags and freight.

A STANDING setting on the driver, not a filter on a search. The list views already had a minimum, but
it was a box typed into the request — so the one surface that speaks first, the lock-screen nudge off
a GPS fix, had nothing to read and applied none. A driver could set a minimum, watch the list obey it,
and still be interrupted at the wheel for a job beneath it.

get.description:
The driver's current shift session (active coupling + vehicle), or { active:false } off duty.

 Carries WHY TODAY WAS QUIET, split by cause. A setting that silences a phone without ever saying so is
 how somebody hears nothing for a week and blames the network — so the two things the network knows and
 was never saying, their own floor and their own rate, travel with the card that shows them.

post.description: Publish a filling tote to the claim marketplace early (before it is full / 24 h).
Sweep: publish every tote that is full or has waited ≥ 24 h.
Register a bulk freight job (trucks only) into the same marketplace as totes.

get.description:
FB1 — the open freight board: the whole market from where the operator is standing.

Every load an operator cannot take comes back MARKED rather than removed, because the loads you cannot
take are the ones that tell you what to buy. `radiusKm` is the OPERATOR's own filter — omit it and the
answer is the entire market, with no 15 km clamp anywhere near it (that number governs interruptions,
and browsing is not an interruption).

parameters.name: radiusKm
parameters.description:
The OPERATOR's own reach, in km. Omit for the whole market — there is no platform clamp here: 15 km is
 right for a lock-screen interruption and wrong for a haulier asking "is it worth 80 km empty?".

parameters.name: driverDid
parameters.description: Whose vehicle to judge against. A driver is pinned to their own; only an operator may name another.

get.description:
FB3b — the open market, to anyone at all.

@Public, and that is the feature. The people who most need to know what freight moves on a corridor are
the ones who do not yet own a truck to move it with: an operator deciding what body to buy, someone
weighing up a move to another city (user, 2026-08-30). Requiring an account to answer that would put the
data behind exactly the door that keeps it from the people it is for.

What is published is the WORK — bodies needed, equipment, weights, both distances, indicative money.
What is not is WHERE any single load sits: a town, a pin rounded to about 5 km, and no code, shop name
or description. Prices are the network's default rate card, and the response says so in `basis` rather
than leaving a client free to render them as offers.

parameters.name: radiusKm
parameters.description: How far the caller cares to look, in km. Omit for the whole market.

get.description:
FB4 — the market series: kilometres of each body ASKED FOR, against kilometres actually MOVED.

 for the same reason the market board is, and more so. The list of open loads is a snapshot
anybody could assemble by watching; this is the shape of a market over time, and it is the thing nobody
else can hold, because it needs both halves — what shippers needed, and what the fleet that exists could
actually take. Giving it away is the moat, not a leak of one (user, 2026-08-30: entrepreneurs should get
that data from us, and that is how we become irreplaceable).

Nothing here identifies a load, a shipper or a driver: it is counts and kilometres, bucketed by truck
body. That is what lets an aggregate be public where the individual rows behind it are coarsened.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Window start, ISO. Defaults to twelve months back — the "yearly km" the series is asked for in.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Window end, ISO. Defaults to now.

get.description:
The fee-response curve: what share of offers at each price were actually taken.

Operator-gated, and not for drivers. It is a picture of how the whole market answers a price, and the
one legitimate use is deciding how dense the node network has to be — not telling any individual what
to charge. A driver's own view of the same machinery is their reach, on their own card.

post.description: A driver names their price for a load posted 'negotiate'. Reserves nothing — the poster's accept claims it.

get.description: The prices offered on a load. Restricted to the side that can act on them — the poster, or an operator.

post.description: The poster takes a price — and that acceptance is what claims the load.
The poster says no to one price. The load, and every other proposal on it, stay open.
A driver pulls back their own price.
Bulk freight pickup (claimed → in_transit). driverDid (the claimer) is verified against claimedBy.
Bulk freight delivery (in_transit → delivered; releases the driver's reserved capacity).
S33b — log a temperature reading for a cold-chain freight in transit (a breach flags it for the tower).

get.description: F3 — a cooperative's own consolidation lots (owner-scoped; an operator must name the owner).

post.description:
F3 — record a member deposit into a lot (auto-posts the freight the moment the lot fills). Owner-scoped
 to the lot's owner (403 for another shop).
F3 — sweep: post every full/aged lot to the marketplace (operator-triggered; a cron would call this).
A driver declares a route A→B → the platform suggests the loads sitting on the way.
Driver GPS heartbeat — updates the vehicle's position on the live fleet map.

get.description:
Fleet-manager dashboard: vehicle/driver/session counts, working hours, live positions + cargo.
A fleet manager sees ONLY their own fleet (actor.tenant); the ?manager= scope and the omit-for-all
view are operator-only. Before S3 anyone could pass ?manager= to read a competitor's fleet.

A driver's JOBS + EARNINGS register (R5): the dedicated-freight hauls they claimed, server-side searched /
 filtered / sorted / paginated → { items, total }. Each row carries the driver's agreed earning (lockedPrice)
 and whether it has been paid. Owner-scoped (403 for another driver).

Running totals for the current filter, and — separately — what has actually been PAID.

They are two different questions and the screen used to answer only one of them under the other's
name. `earned`/`paid`/`unpaid` come from the jobs themselves, where "paid" means the network booked
what it owes at the moment of delivery. `settlement` comes from the payouts, where paid means a rail
confirmed money leaving. Until settlement existed there was nothing to tell apart; now there is, and
conflating them would tell somebody they have their money when it is still in the sister's account.
Export the whole matching set (every page, current filters) as CSV — the driver's OWN earnings export. Owner-scoped.

post.description: Driver accepts a suggestion → reserves the load + its weight against the vehicle's capacity.
Driver declines a suggestion.

Decline an offer straight from the notification's "Not now", using the one-shot capability that rode in
the push. PUBLIC by necessity and safe by construction: the service worker handling that tap has no
session, and the alternative — handing a background script the driver's token — trades a one-word
problem for their whole identity. The token is unguessable, bound to a single offer, single-use, and
dead when the offer lapses (see mintDeclineToken). It carries no authority to claim anything.

Enroll (or return) the consumer for an OTP-verified phone; optionally set the PIN in the same step.
Requires the phone to have been verified via `sbg/auth/phone/verify` first — the OTP is the identity
proof; enroll consumes it (one verification → one enrolment), so a stale verification can't be reused.
Reopen the app: phone + 4-digit PIN, no OTP (locks after repeated wrong PINs — then OTP again).
Set or change the signed-in person's PIN.

get.description: The signed-in person + every role they hold (the role switcher reads this) + their self profile.

patch.description: Set the signed-in person's own display name and/or avatar (S29). Returns the updated self-view.

post.description: "Act as" a held role → an actor token carrying that role's scopes + tenant.

get.description:
The receiver/sender home: every parcel this person is a party to (sent + received), matched by their
verified phone — retroactively (O4). PII-free authenticated twins; the counterpart stays hashed. S32d
also returns `freights` — any order of theirs that was too big for the parcel network and diverted to
dedicated freight, so a diverted order never vanishes from the buyer's home.

post.description:
PG1 — parcel genesis from the sender's own phone: the IDENTICAL mint the vendor console gets (derived
size + cargo gate, locked price, shipment DID + twin + planned journey + printable label at creation).
Cash at the counter: the price locks NOW and the shop collects it at drop-off — so the label (the
sender's drop-off credential) issues immediately. The sender's identity comes from the TOKEN, never
the body. A P4+ load is REFUSED here (not diverted like a vendor's): the freight lane bills a shipper
at claim through the vendor prepaid rail, and a person has no billing rail yet — a silent divert would
be un-priced, un-consented free freight (the driver still gets paid). Refusing keeps the money
invariant; the Send UI explains and points at a PUDO shop.

get.description: One parcel the caller is a party to — the authenticated twin + status timeline (404 to a non-party).

post.description: The receiver attaches their own delivered-state photo (proof of what they received) — S23.

The receiver answers the final notice — the four things a person can do about a closed window.

On their OWN parcel only, and 404 otherwise: this is the one screen in the network where somebody
can give up a claim to goods, so it must not be possible to do it to somebody else's.

Returns their twin rather than a bare acknowledgement, because three of the four choices change what
the app should be showing them and a screen that has to guess will guess wrong.

The receiver names somebody to collect for them.

The code comes BACK to the receiver, which is the point: they are the one who has to pass it on, and
a code the network delivered straight to the neighbour would be the network deciding who a person
trusts. Their own code keeps working alongside it, and the shop still learns neither.

The receiver rates the STORE they bought from — stars and tags, on a parcel we actually carried.

That last part is the whole point: a public review site cannot tell a real customer from a paid one,
and we can, because we moved the parcel. Verified beats volume. One verdict per shipment, so nobody
can stack a merchant either way, and only after delivery — an opinion about a parcel that has not
arrived is an opinion about waiting, which the measured half already reports better.
The receiver files a delivery dispute (reason + photo) → routed to the vendor / sender + control tower.
Create (or return) an invite for a contact → a token the app turns into a shareable /send/ link (S24).

get.description: The inviter's sent invites + how many turned into joins (the growth credit) — PII-free.
The invite landing check — validates the token without exposing the inviter or the invitee.

post.description: Upload one downscaled image (+ optional thumbnail). The owner is the authenticated caller.

get.description: The caller's own media — the source for the media library (S27). PII-free projection.
Stream one image's bytes (or its thumbnail via ?variant=thumb). Owner-or-operator only.

delete.description: Remove one of your own asset images early (vehicle/trailer only — evidence bins stay locked).

get.description:
Every option of one vocabulary, with the picture where one is curated.

The whole topic in one request, deliberately: a picker needs all of it to render, and the "not sure"
sheet shows every option side by side. One request per option would make that sheet a waterfall on the
exact connection least able to afford it.

One option's illustration bytes.

PUBLIC and immutable-cacheable: the URL carries the blob id as `?v=`, so a replaced picture is a new URL
and the old one can be cached hard without ever going stale. nosniff because these bytes are served to
a browser — the upload path already refuses anything whose magic number is not a real raster image.

put.description: Set or replace one option's illustration. Operator-only — see the class note.

delete.description: Remove one option's illustration. The option stays; its sheet falls back to text alone.

get.description: The `applicationServerKey` the browser needs to build a PushSubscription. Public, not a secret.

post.description: Enrol this device (the browser's PushSubscription) for the authenticated owner.

delete.description: Drop this device (the browser unsubscribed, or the user turned notifications off).

post.description: Send a test push to every device the owner has enrolled — the "it works" confirmation after opt-in.

get.description: The caller's notification inbox (newest first) + the unread count — the in-app notification centre (N2).

post.description: Mark one of the caller's notifications read. Ownership-guarded in the service.
Mark all of the caller's notifications read (clears the bell badge).

What would this cost to ship? Creates nothing — no parcel, no account, no reservation.

The one call the "calculate your shipping fee" button makes. A key is optional: send one in
`X-SBG-Key` and the limit becomes yours rather than your IP's, and a server-side key also returns the
costed breakdown.

Turn a price into a shipment. Needs a SECRET key: a credential that ships things must never sit in a
page. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header and the same name is spent at most once, however many times a
flaky network makes you ask.

A TEST key runs every check and creates nothing — see ShippingApiService.mint.

get.description:
Where the network can deliver: every country it operates in and the areas inside it that have a
collection point somebody can actually stand at. What a destination picker is built from.

Where is my shipment? The state of one you created, read back by the key that created it.

The price comes off the parcel, not from a fresh quote: re-pricing a sold shipment would have this
endpoint disagree with the merchant's own invoice. Somebody else's shipment answers NOT FOUND rather
than FORBIDDEN — "you may not see this" tells a stranger the id is real.

The collection code is NOT here. It arrives on the `ready_for_pickup` callback, at the moment it is
useful and to an endpoint the store registered; on a pollable read it would sit in every log file that
ever recorded a response body.

post.description:
Call it off, while it still can be.

A secret key, for the reason minting needs one: a credential that can undo a shipment must never sit
in a page. The window is the network's own — Created, At_PUDO or At_MDP — and once somebody is
carrying it, calling it off is a conversation rather than an API call.

THERE IS NO AMEND, deliberately. Moving a parcel's destination or changing its size changes what it
costs, and an "edit" that quietly re-prices something a buyer already paid for is the worst possible
version of this call. Cancel and create the replacement, so the new price is seen and agreed.

get.description: Triple-entry journal + chain verification (SSE-082).

info.title: SeeBuyGet API
info.description: SeeBuyGet — see, buy, get. The API behind the SeeBuyGet network: the PUDO pick-up/drop-off agents, drivers, fleets and MDP sort hubs that move a parcel, plus the seebuyget.com consumer web (storefront, checkout, tracking). Authenticate with the actor token minted at login.

consolidationSlots.description: Labels (e.g. "Green-3") the agent designates as consolidation/bundle slots for small parcels.

country.description: The country the shop stands in (ISO-3166 alpha-2). Omitted = this deployment's home country.

The country this shop stands in (ISO-3166 alpha-2). It decides which sister contracts it, and a
 journey that leaves it crosses a border. Absent on every pre-slice record, which reads as this
 deployment's home country — read it through AgentService.countryOf, never off the field.

entityId.description:
The sister company this shop is contracted to — it buys the shop's handling and owes it the fee.
 A shop sits in exactly one country, so this is unambiguous. Absent on pre-entity records; read it
 through AgentService.entityIdOf().
The sister that owes it. Its books are where the drawdown posts.

payeeDid.description:
WHO IS PAID — the party the network contracts with: a fleet, a courier, a hub. Never a person who
 merely did the work; see DriverService.payeeOf.

day.description:
The settlement day this covers, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

The idempotency key, with the payee: a run that fires twice — a retry, two operators, a cron that
overlaps itself — must not pay the same day's work twice. Same-day settlement is a promise about
WHEN, so the day is the natural unit rather than a batch id nobody can reason about.

providerRef.description: The rail's own reference. The thing you quote when somebody says they were not paid.

entryId.description: The journal entry that moved the money. Present ONLY once settled — before that nothing has moved.

reversalEntryId.description: …and the entry that moved it back, if it bounced.

jurisdiction.description:
ISO-3166-alpha-2. Required for a sister (it is what makes it the merchant of record there);
 absent on the group, whose country of incorporation nothing in the system depends on.

currency.description:
The currency this entity settles in, derived from its jurisdiction. A group has none: it holds
 no custody account, so there is no balance for a currency to describe.

feePct.description:
The margin this sister charges on top of provider costs, as a fraction (0.02 = 2%). A knob each
market turns for itself rather than a constant of the network — Nairobi and Amsterdam do not have to
price alike. Absent means "the network default"; read it through EntityService.feePctOf(), never
off the record, so a sister created before the knob existed still answers.

SUPERSEDED BY `rates` and kept as its input: a sister that only ever set this one number is read as
having set that number as its MARGIN. It is not migrated on write, because a value that rewrites
itself the first time anything reads it makes the record's history unreadable.

rates.description:
What this sister charges, in the three layers a business actually decides separately.

One blended percentage cannot answer "are we earning because the market is good, or because we are
carrying risk nobody is paying us for?" — and that is the question the knobs exist to answer.

ratesByLane.description:
Per-lane overrides, keyed by the CALLER'S vocabulary (today a CargoLane: pudo | mdp | dedicated).

A plain string map because the lane taxonomy belongs to the pudo module and this is foundation — the
books must not learn what a parcel is in order to hold a number. The caller validates the key; this
only ever validates the rates.

Absent lane → the sister's own `rates` → `feePct` as a margin → the network default. Four steps, each
one a real state some sister is in.

taxRegistration.description:
The registration this sister collects tax under — its VAT/TIN/GST number in its own country.

Not the same thing as being incorporated there, which `jurisdiction` already says: a company can be
registered to trade and not registered to collect, and below a turnover threshold that is the normal
state. So this is separate, and absent means "not registered to collect" rather than "unknown".

tax.description:
What this sister charges in tax on everything it sells. Absent means none — the network default, and
the state every sister is in until an operator deliberately says otherwise.

taxByLane.description:
Per-lane tax overrides, keyed by the caller's vocabulary exactly as `ratesByLane` is.

Here for a reason narrower than it looks: tax rates vary by what is SUPPLIED, and lane is the only
supply-type axis this system has. A jurisdiction that zero-rates one kind of transport and standard-
rates another can express that; everyone else sets one rate and never touches this.

insurance.description:
What this sister covers when it breaks something, and what it charges to cover more.

Absent means the network default — no free cover and no premium charged, which is where every sister
starts. Read it through EntityService.insuranceFor(), never off the record.

parentEntityId.description: Sisters point at the group they belong to.

lane.description: Which kind of work this applies to. Omitted = the sister's default for everything.

costOfRiskPct.description: What carrying the exposure costs — an insurance premium, or the provision standing in for one.

profitOnRiskPct.description: What the sister earns for choosing to carry it — where a specialised vehicle pays itself back.

marginPct.description: The general company layer, on everything.

lane.description: Which kind of work this applies to. Omitted = the sister's default for everything.

ratePct.description: As a FRACTION — sixteen percent is 0.16, not 16. Bounds are enforced in the service.

label.description: What the authority calls it: 'VAT', 'GST'. The network has no default worth having.

registration.description: The number this sister collects under. Required before any rate above zero will be accepted.

lane.description: Which kind of work this applies to. Omitted = the sister's default for everything.

premiumPct.description: Charged on the declared value ABOVE the free limit, as a FRACTION — two percent is 0.02.

freeLimit.description: Covered on every shipment without anybody declaring anything, in the sister's own currency.

currency.description:
What the amount IS. Optional only because rows written before this field existed have none — read
 it through agentLedgerCurrencyOf(), which defaults them, never straight off the record.

entryId.description:
The journal entry this row projects. The BOOKS are the money; this row is how a shopkeeper reads
 it. Absent on rows written before the books existed, and on records that move no money of ours.

natureCode.description: S30 — the commodity's primary cargo nature (default GEN). Drives the compatibility matrix.

state.description: Open until an operator decides. This is the field that makes `Disputed` a queue rather than a grave.

fromStatus.description:
The status the parcel held when the dispute was raised, restored when the case closes. Stored
 rather than inferred: a rejected counter dispute must leave the parcel collectable again, and
 guessing that from the origin would be one assumption away from stranding somebody's goods.

raisedBy.description: Who reported it — an agent DID at a counter, a person DID from the app.

award.description:
What was awarded, in the parcel's own currency. Zero on a rejection, and zero is a real answer
 that still gets recorded — a refusal a claimant can be shown beats a case that went quiet.

note.description:
The operator's reasoning. REQUIRED on every decision including a rejection: a person whose goods
 arrived broken is owed an explanation even when they are not owed money.

atId.description: Whose place it was: an agent DID, a vendorId, or the sender's own DID.

originAgentDid.description:
The first PUDO to take custody — absent when there is none, which is a real case rather than missing
data: a store collected from its own dock hands the parcel straight to a driver. This is NOT where the
parcel came from; that is `birthplace`, which every parcel has. The two were one field until they had
to be told apart.

collectingEntityId.description:
R1 — the sister company that collects for this shipment: the one in the PAYER's jurisdiction. A
vendor order is paid by the store, so it is the store's sister; a walk-up is paid at the counter,
so it is the origin shop's. Never the group, which is not a party to customer transactions.
Internal: it is an accounting fact, and appears on no consumer or public surface.

otp.description:
Release secret. The destination agent reads it aloud from their screen and the customer repeats
it back — it is never SMS'd, so it costs nothing and works with no signal. Because it is the
sole custody check, wrong attempts are counted and the code is burned at OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS.

otpAttempts.description:
Wrong-attempt counter for whichever release secret this parcel uses — the OTP above on a peer-send,
the collectionCode below on an inbound order. A parcel has exactly one live secret, so one budget
guards both paths; it is reset when the secret becomes live (arrive() / shelve()) and by a reissue.

otpLockedAt.description: Set when the release secret was burned by repeated wrong attempts; release needs an operator reissue.

transportFactor.description:
The SIZE FACTOR its transport was quoted at, stamped at mint for the same reason. A network constant
 today, but one that will be retuned — and the flexible rebate recomputes the real cost at delivery,
 so an unstamped factor would re-price parcels already sold. Absent on records written before this
 field existed; read it through ParcelService.transportFactorOf, which falls back to the constant.

shipmentProvision.description:
The COST-OF-RISK slice of the platform fee on this shipment — money set aside against claims rather
than earned, stamped at mint like everything else about the price.

Inside `platformFee`, never on top of it: the customer paid this the day the rate stack shipped, and
moving it from revenue to a provision changes no price. Stamped because a sister that turns its
cost-of-risk knob tomorrow must not change what was set aside for a shipment sold today — and
because a refund has to release exactly what a billing set aside.

Absent means ZERO, the same reading as tax: a shipment sold before any of this carried no cover.

declaredValue.description:
THE COVER on this shipment, stamped at mint.

`coverLimit` is the ceiling an upheld damage award is checked against — the free limit the selling
sister carries, or the value the shipper declared, whichever is higher. Declaring less than the free
limit does not reduce cover: the floor is a floor, not a swap.

`shipmentPremium` is what was charged for the part above the free limit, and like the cost-of-risk
slice it accrues to the claims provision rather than to revenue — money collected against a promise,
not earned for a service performed.

Stamped, so a sister that changes its policy tomorrow cannot change what it promised on a shipment
sold today. Absent on every parcel from before this existed, which reads as NO cover — the honest
answer, because none was priced, promised or paid for.

currency.description:
The money every figure above is in — the SELLING sister's, stamped at mint. Absent on records
 written before prices named their unit; read it through ParcelService.currencyOf.

customs.description:
The paperwork this parcel crosses a border with. Absent on a domestic shipment, which needs none —
 and never absent on one that crosses, because the mint refuses to sell that shipment without it.

sellerEntityId.description:
The sister that SOLD this shipment: it collected the price and carries the cost of every leg, so a
 shop in another country that handles this parcel recharges its own sister's outlay to this one, at
 cost. Absent on records written before a parcel named its seller — then nobody recharges anybody,
 which is exactly right for a single-sister world.

fx.description:
The exchange rates this parcel's price was struck at, when it needed any.

 Kept for the same reason `platformFeePct` is: a price is a promise made at a moment, and the rate
 behind it moves. Without this, a cross-border parcel's cost is a number nobody can reconstruct or
 argue about, and the sister that collected it could not later prove what it owed the sister that
 performed the leg. Absent on every domestic parcel, because nothing was converted.

ceilingProvision.description:
…and the cover inside that ceiling, for the same reason: the rebate has to release exactly the
 provision the ceiling set aside, and re-deriving it from a rate would land a cent away.

readyAt.description:
When it became collectable — the moment it hit the destination shelf.

Stamped rather than derived from the last scan, and the difference is not cosmetic: a wrong
collection code writes a `Ready_For_Pickup` scan of its own, so ageing off the scan list would reset
the uncollected clock every time somebody fumbled their code. The one event that matters here happens
once, so it is recorded once.

Absent on records written before this existed; readers fall back to the scan list.

uncollectedRemindedAt.description:
When the receiver was reminded it was still waiting. Set once — see the dispatcher for why one
 reminder and not a series — and set even when there was nobody to tell, so somebody who signs up
 later is not greeted by a nudge about a parcel that has been sitting a fortnight.

returnParcelId.description:
The journey home, for a parcel nobody came for. Present only on a 'Returned' one — the two read as
 one story rather than as an abandonment and an unexplained new shipment.

unclaimedAt.description:
When the free collection window ran out — the start of the holding-fee clock.

Distinct from readyAt, and the distinction is the whole feature: readyAt is when the wait began,
this is when the wait stopped being free. An extension resets readyAt and CLEARS this, because a
receiver who bought more time is inside a free window again by definition.

holdingSettled.description: Holding already settled, so a part-paid parcel is not billed twice at the counter.

extensionsUsed.description: Extensions taken. The first is free (FREE_EXTENSIONS); counted so the second can be priced.

receiverResponse.description:
What the receiver said when told the window had closed. Absent means silence — which is the
 common case and an outcome the whole flow has to reach correctly without.

collectProxy.description:
Somebody named to collect instead of the receiver. Their code releases the parcel; so does the
 receiver's own, because nominating a neighbour does not stop you collecting it yourself.

relinquishedAt.description:
When the RECEIVER gave up their claim to the goods.

Only the receiver can set this: sender owns the shipment, receiver owns the goods, so the receiver
is the only party with anything to relinquish. It does not make the box disappear — there is a real
parcel in a real shop — and it is not 'Voided', which would say the shipment never happened when it
happened all the way. It moves the parcel into the disposal queue, and only once no store still has
a funded claim to bring it home.

birthplace.description: Where it came into being. Absent on pre-slice records — read it through `birthplaceOf`.

custody.description: Who has physically held it, in order. Absent on pre-slice records — read through `custodianOf`.

packaging.description:
FB5 — how the goods are PACKED, which decides the body and what has to lift it. Omitted falls back to
 the DEPLOYMENT's default (sacks here, loose in a European deployment), never to a network-wide guess.

excludedBodies.description:
FB2d — bodies the SHIPPER rules out. At a counter the walk-in customer IS the shipper, so this is their
 call to make and the clerk's job only to record it. A PREFERENCE, not a limit of any vehicle: the board
 shows it as the shipper's choice, and it binds a claim only because the driver was told first.

bodyHint.description:
FB2c — what the shop THINKS the load needs. ADVISORY by decision: recorded, shown and counted, never
 matched on, because a clerk cannot reliably tell a skeletal from a flatbed and a binding wrong pick
 would exclude the one operator who could have carried it.

recoverAboveValue.description:
The goods value above which this store wants an uncollected parcel shipped back to it. Omitted =
 never offer; 0 = always ask. Two different statements, and both are real.

ownerPhone.description:
The store operator's phone (S20). When present, this vendor is linked to the operator's person
 identity so the same human can also send, receive or drive under one account — never a duplicate.

recoverAboveValue.description:
The goods value above which this store wants an UNCOLLECTED parcel shipped back to it.

A store's own arithmetic, pre-declared so nobody has to be asked while a shelf slot sits occupied:
what the goods are worth against what the return leg costs. Below it, getting the box back is worth
less than the journey and the store would rather not pay for it.

Undefined = never offer, which is the safe default: a store that has said nothing has not agreed to
be billed for anything. Zero means "always offer", which is a different statement and a real one.

NOTE what this is NOT. It does not let a store abandon anything — the buyer paid for the goods, so
they are the buyer's (see the parcel-trunk rule). This decides only whether the store is OFFERED the
chance to pay for its return.

did.description: Real GLOS DID (S15). The vendorId stays the domain key; the DID is what an actor token binds to.

collection.description: Their own dock, if they have asked for one. Absent = they drop off at a PUDO like everyone else.

contactMobile.description:
Somebody to tell when a parcel is coming BACK.

A store is a counterparty on the outbound leg and a RECEIVER on a return, and a receiver the network
cannot reach is a parcel that arrives at a shop with nobody expecting it. Taken from the operator's
phone at registration, where it is already asked for.

country.description: The country the dock stands in. Omitted = the store's own — a warehouse abroad says so.

sealRequired.description:
A SHOP bag, published by the shopkeeper's SEAL and by nothing else. A hub bag has no seal step, so the
dispatch sweep publishes it the moment it is full or aged; a shop bag that the sweep published behind
the counter would advertise a bag still open on the floor — and lock the shop out of the completeness
gate, which only accepts a filling bag. The sweep asks the shop to close it instead (see publishReady).
Undefined on a hub bag and on every pre-slice record, which is the correct default for both.

sealPromptedFor.description: Which nudge this shop has already had for this bag, so the sweep asks once per reason (full → aged).

sealedAt.description: When the shop closed it. The record that the completeness gate ran, distinct from being published.

haul.description:
What carrying this bag is worth, LOCKED AT CLAIM — the tote analogue of a freight's `lockedPrice`.

Locked rather than computed at delivery for the same reason freight locks: the driver agreed to a job
whose distance and contents were what they were at that moment. A parcel added after they claimed, or a
destination re-pointed by a re-sort, must not silently rewrite what they are owed either way.

Absent on a bag nobody claimed through the marketplace (it can still be loaded), and on every record
written before this existed — both settle on the handling fee alone, and `basis` says which.

fromAgentDid.description: Where it is now — the shop holding it — and where it would go back to.

declaredValue.description: What the goods are worth, and what the journey home costs. The store's arithmetic, shown not implied.

holdingCost.description:
What the shop is owed for having held the slot since the window closed — recomputed on every read,
never stamped.

The transport half is a held price a store is billed exactly what it was shown. This half is a
METER, and showing it as though it were fixed would be the one dishonest number on the screen. It
grows while they think about it, which is also the truest pressure this feature has: a store
watching the cost of deciding nothing go up is being told something real.

quoteId.description: The held price this will be billed at. A store is billed the figure it was shown.

returnParcelId.description: The return shipment, once it exists.

did.description: Real GLOS DID (S2). The mdpId stays the domain key; the DID is what an actor token binds to.

country.description:
The country this hub stands in — same fact as a shop's, and it matters more here: a hub is where a
 cross-border journey changes hands, so the leg into it is the one that clears customs. Absent on
 pre-slice records; read it through MdpService.countryOf.

entityId.description:
The sister company this hub is contracted to — same reasoning as a shop's: a fixed site sits in
 one country. Absent on pre-entity records; read it through MdpService.entityIdOf().

natureCode.description: S30 — the commodity's primary cargo nature (default GEN). Drives the compatibility matrix.

country.description: The country the hub stands in. A hub may serve zones across a border; it stands in one country.

jurisdiction.description: Country of incorporation (ISO-3166-alpha-2) — the sister that contracts and pays this fleet.

Country of incorporation — which sister company contracts and pays this fleet, and in what
currency. A fleet is paid as a SUPPLIER, one invoice in one currency; how it then pays its own
drivers, in which countries, under whose employment law, is entirely the fleet's business.

entityId.description:
That sister, by id. Absent on records written before entities existed — read it through
 FleetManagerService.entityIdOf(), which resolves from the jurisdiction.

jurisdiction.description:
Legal residence (ISO-3166-alpha-2) — for an INDEPENDENT courier, who the network pays directly.
 Ignored when managerDid is set: the fleet is paid, and its drivers are the fleet's business.

portrait.description: Their face, for the badge — see DriverPortrait. Absent is ordinary, never a blocker.

entityId.description: The sister that contracts this courier directly. Absent for a fleet-attached driver.

nudgeMinEarn.description:
Do not interrupt this driver for work paying less than this, all in.

It lives on the DRIVER, not on the coupling, unlike the snooze and the derived-leg switch beside it.
Those two are moods held for a shift — a puncture, a favour taken this morning — and it is right that
ending the shift ends them. A fee floor is not a mood: it is the driver's cost base, and fuel does not
get cheaper because yesterday finished. Asking for it again every morning would make it the thing it
replaced — a number typed into a search box that dies on the next reload.

The price of standing is that it can starve somebody silently, which is exactly what the snooze warns
about. That is paid for by COUNTING what it suppresses and showing them (see DispatchService's floor
report): a setting you can watch working is a setting you can undo.

Absent, or zero, means no floor. Bounded by MAX_NUDGE_MIN_EARN.

photoRef.description: The driver's face for their badge — optional by design; see DriverPortrait.

leg.description: Where they are going. Optional: a driver may couple first and say afterwards.

snoozedUntil.description:
New offers are SNOOZED until this instant (absent = taking work).

A rider needs this far more than a line-haul driver does: lunch, a fare of their own, a puncture, the
last hour of a long day. It stops NEW work only — everything already claimed is still theirs to carry,
hand over and deliver, because snoozing offers is not going off shift. It lives on the coupling, so
ending the shift ends it: nobody discovers tomorrow morning that they are still snoozed.

derivedLegOff.description:
The driver has switched OFF the road we worked out from the load they took.

One decision, honoured for the rest of the shift. Without it, turning it off would clear a road that
the very next claim puts straight back — which is not a switch, it is an argument. Like the snooze
beside it, it lives on the coupling, so ending the shift ends it.

leg.description: The leg for this shift, declared in the same breath as picking the vehicle.

packaging.description:
FB5 — how the goods are PACKED, which decides the body and what has to lift it. Omitted falls back to
 the DEPLOYMENT's default (sacks here, loose in a European deployment), never to a network-wide guess.

excludedBodies.description:
Bodies the SHIPPER rules out (theft risk, an insurer's wording, a customer's requirement). A stated
 preference, not a physical constraint, and the board presents it as one.

commitMode.description:
FB0c — 'negotiate' posts the load for a price to be agreed BEFORE anyone commits: drivers send their
 number, the poster accepts one, and only that acceptance claims it. Absent = 'instant', the behaviour
 every load has had until now. A negotiate load is deliberately kept out of the push offers and nudges,
 which exist to be answered with a single Claim tap.

dimensionsCm.description:
FB0b — the load's measurements. Optional: loose bulk genuinely has none (a tipper-load of sand has a
 weight and no shape), and a bulletin freight may be posted before anyone has measured it. Supplied, they
 are STORED — until FB0b they were read to classify the cargo and then discarded, which is why nothing
 downstream could answer "does this fit a flatbed rather than a box body".

indivisible.description:
Can it be split into two smaller loads? A divisible 30 t is two ordinary trips; an indivisible 30 t is a
 low-loader and a permit.

bodyHint.description:
The minter's own body pick — ADVISORY. Recorded and shown, never used to match: a wrong pick would
 silently exclude the operator who could have taken the load.

natureCode.description: S32 — the freight's primary cargo nature (default GEN); drives the required vehicle capability.

scheduledPickupAt.description:
F1 — a FUTURE pickup date: the load is booked for later. Must be a full datetime WITH an offset (Z or
 ±HH:MM) so the instant is unambiguous — a date-only or offset-less string would resolve to a server-
 timezone-dependent moment. Absent = ship now.

allowEarlyClaim.description:
F1 — the shipper's early-claim choice for a scheduled load: true (default) → a driver may RESERVE it
 ahead of its pickup date; false → it stays out of the marketplace until due.

truckSubtype.description: The truck body. Absent for a vehicle class that has no subtype — a van is a van.

bodyHint.description:
The minter's own body pick. ADVISORY — shown, compared and counted, NEVER used to filter (user, 2026-08-30).
 A shop clerk booking a walk-up cannot reliably tell a skeletal from a flatbed, and a binding wrong pick
 would invisibly exclude the one operator who could have taken the load. Where it disagrees with the
 derived body, that disagreement is itself a market signal worth reporting.

excludedBodies.description:
Bodies the SHIPPER rules out — theft risk, an insurer's wording, a customer's requirement. A PREFERENCE,
 and typed as one: the board says "the shipper ruled out open bodies", never dressing it up as physics.

packaging.description:
FB5 — how the goods are PRESENTED for handling, which is what decides the body and the kit.

Recorded per consignment rather than inferred from the commodity, because the same commodity is handled
completely differently from place to place (user, 2026-08-30): sugar is poured into a food-grade bulk
trailer in Holland and stacked in sacks on a flatbed in Kenya. A rule keyed on "is it sugar" gets one of
those two wrong wherever it is deployed.

priceOrigin.description:
FB0c — where lockedPrice came from. 'computed' (or absent, for anything locked before FB0c) means it IS
 priceBreakdown.total. 'negotiated' means two parties agreed a number, so lockedPrice is authoritative and
 may differ from the breakdown — which is kept anyway, because its distances are real and are what the
 market series reads. Every money path already reads lockedPrice; nothing bills off the breakdown.

commitMode.description:
FB0c — how this load may be taken. 'instant' (the default, and what every pre-FB0c load is read as) means
 a fit driver claims it at the computed price. 'negotiate' means the minter wants to agree a price first:
 drivers PROPOSE, the poster accepts one, and only that acceptance claims the load.

indivisible.description:
Can the load be split into two smaller ones? The single most decision-changing fact about anything
 oversize: a divisible 30 t is two ordinary trips, an indivisible 30 t is a low-loader and a permit.

bodyDerived.description:
FB0b — the body this load canonically needs, STAMPED at registration (and the basis it was derived on).
 Frozen rather than computed on read for the same reason a price is frozen at claim: "kilometres of
 flatbed offered in 2026" must not change when someone tunes a threshold in 2027. Absent on a pre-FB0b
 freight, which is derived live and reports itself as weight-only.

bulk.description:
DERIVED from packaging (`loose`), and kept because vehicle matching is written against it.

It used to be the stored truth and it meant two opposite things — "loose, it tips or augers" in the body
derivation, "sugar/cement bags" in the vehicle spec. It now has exactly one meaning, the loose one, which
is what `Vehicle.carriesBulk` and the board's NO_BULK_BODY blocker already assumed.

equipmentGaps.description:
S32c — the ends whose SITE cannot handle this cargo (no qualifying load/unload equipment on hand). An
 ADVISORY flag ("arrange a forklift at the destination"), not a block — a Local Admin resolves it. Empty
 when both ends are equipped (or their equipment is unknown, e.g. a bulletin freight with only geo labels).

postedByDid.description:
FB0c — who posted the load, and therefore who negotiates for it. Distinct from shipperDid, which is who
 PAYS: a counter booking deliberately has no shipperDid (the customer's cash settles off-platform) yet
 still has a shop that must be able to answer a proposal. Absent for a bulletin freight → operators only.

carriedBy.description:
FB4a — what actually CARRIED it, stamped at claim. The mirror of `bodyDerived`: that one records the body
the load needed, this one the body that turned up.

Frozen for exactly the reason the derived body and the price are frozen. Only `claimedBy` was ever
recorded, so "kilometres moved by container chassis in 2026" could only be answered by looking up what
that driver is coupled to TODAY — and a driver who sells a flatbed and buys a box van would silently
rewrite every haul they have ever done. A market series that changes retroactively is not a series.

Absent on a load claimed before FB4a, and on one whose claimer had no truck subtype (a van or a bus).
Such a haul is counted as UNKNOWN in the analytics, never attributed to a body by inference.

code.description: Stable machine code — a screen switches on this, never on the message.

message.description: The English sentence. Not yet translated; the codes exist so it can be, without moving the logic.

bodyDerived.description: What body the load needs, and how strong that claim is (measured, or guessed from weight alone).

deadheadKm.description: The empty run to reach it, the paid run, and their sum — the numbers the whole decision turns on.

price.description: Indicative, priced against THIS driver's vehicle. Absent when they are not coupled to one.

earningsPerKm.description:
Earnings per TOTAL kilometre, empty run included — the board's sort key. Null when it cannot be computed
 (no vehicle, or a zero-distance job): an unsortable row is shown as unsortable, never floated to the top.

canTake.description: True when nothing but an 'unknown' stands in the way.

requiredEquipment.description: Kit a vehicle must have to load and unload it — the other half of the investment question.

area.description:
Coarse: the nearest town we know, not the pickup's own label. Absent where nothing is near enough
 to name honestly — a distance with no name beats a name that implies precision we do not have.

destArea.description: Likewise for the far end: what corridor this load runs, in towns.

pickupAbout.description: Rounded to ~0.05° (≈5 km) so the market can be mapped without a load being met at its gate.

bodyDerived.description:
The body this load needs and how strong that claim is. THE field the whole page exists for: it is what
 turns "there is work here" into "there is work here for a flatbed".

deadheadKm.description: From the point the caller asked about — their question, not ours.

indicativeTotal.description:
INDICATIVE ONLY, and named so. Computed at the network's default rate for a typical vehicle, because
 an anonymous caller has no vehicle whose rate card we could price against. What an actual operator
 earns is their own rate on their own corridor — this is the market's shape, not an offer.

indicativePerKm.description: Indicative earnings per TOTAL kilometre, empty run included. Null when it cannot be computed.

basis.description:
Said in the payload, not just in the docs: every price here is the network default applied to this
 load, so a client cannot render these numbers as an offer without stepping over the word.

offeredLoads.description: Loads POSTED in the window whose derived body is this one.

offeredKm.description: Their LOADED kilometres — pickup → dropoff. Work asked for; empty running is never in here.

offeredMeasured.description:
How many of those had a MEASURED body rather than one guessed from weight. The rest still count; they
 are a softer claim, and a reader investing against this is entitled to know the difference.

movedLoads.description: Loads CLAIMED in the window and carried by a vehicle of this body.

movedKm.description: Their loaded kilometres. THE number — "km of containers moved".

deadheadKm.description:
The empty run to reach that work. Beside movedKm, never inside it: a market whose fleet turns 40% of its
 wheels empty is a different investment from one that does not, and only a separate figure says so.

unmetLoads.description:
Loads posted in the window that NOTHING ever claimed — demand the fleet did not meet. The gap between
 this and the moved figures is the sentence somebody deciding what to buy is actually paying for.

from.description:
The window these figures cover, echoed as ISO instants. A kilometre count means nothing without the
 period it accrued over, and "yearly km" is a rate a reader has to be able to check for themselves.

maxSpend.description: The cash cap the customer agreed — what a price is judged against.

openProposals.description: How many prices are waiting for an answer. The whole reason this row is on a screen.

agreedPrice.description: Set once the load is taken, so the poster sees the outcome without a second call.

price.description: The DRIVER's earning being asked for (not the shipper's all-in charge).

note.description: The case for the number, in the driver's own words.

price.description: The DRIVER's earning they are asking for — the same quantity as lockedPrice, not the shipper's charge.

note.description: The driver's case for the number, in their own words ("I'm empty-running past your gate on Thursday").

deadheadKm.description:
The two legs AS AT the proposal, from the position the driver proposed from. Carried so the accepted
 haul records a real deadhead/loaded split rather than one invented at acceptance time.

destLocation.description:
Where the load is going, as a place — so a driver can see and navigate the whole leg rather than only
 the trip to the pickup. Absent when the destination cannot be resolved to a coordinate.

collectMin.description:
WHAT THIS JOB COSTS THE DRIVER, IN MINUTES — the two figures a decision at the wheel is actually made
on, and the pair `detourKm` could never give.

`collectMin` is the extra time to go and get it. `deliverMin` is the extra time that CARRYING it then
costs, on top of that — because a pickup next door whose destination is an hour the wrong way is not a
small job, and a kilometre figure computed over the pickup alone said it was.

Time rather than distance because that is the unit a driver spends and the only one they can explain
to anybody else: a bus driver cannot justify eight kilometres to a bus full of passengers, but "this
costs you six minutes" is a sentence everybody in the vehicle understands.

Both are measured against the road the driver DECLARED, so they are genuinely extra. With no declared
road there is nothing to be extra to, and they report the plain travel time instead — which is the
honest reading: when you have no plan, all of it is extra.

`deliverMin` is absent when the destination cannot be placed. Never guessed: a made-up minute is worse
than a missing one, because this is the number somebody agrees to.

price.description:
S34 — the priced offer: the driver's earning + the transparent B + D·R·M breakdown. FREIGHT ONLY —
 a bag has no B + D·R·M, so read `earn` for the figure that covers both kinds.

earn.description:
WHAT THIS JOB PAYS, all in — the one number the driver is agreeing to, for either kind of load.

Freight: the same figure as `price.total`. A bag: the handling fee plus the road it will travel.

It exists because a bag's pay stopped being a constant. Every surface used to hard-code the flat
loading fee, which was true then and became a LIE the moment distance and contents entered the
arithmetic — understating a real job on the very screen where somebody says yes to it. Indicative
here, against this driver's current vehicle; locked at claim, exactly as a freight's price is.

parcels.description:
BAGS ONLY — what the earning is made of: how many parcels are inside, and how full the bag is. See
 Claimable.parcels for why a figure without them is a figure taken on trust.

inviteToken.description: S24: if the person arrived via an invite link, credit the inviter on first join.

expectedTotal.description:
The locked total the sender consented to at the quote step. If the market moved before mint, the
 server rejects with PRICE_CHANGED (carrying the fresh total) so the app can re-confirm — never
 silently bill a different amount than the one shown.

pointId.description: A collection point by its public id — exact, and what a merchant's checkout already holds.

address.description: …or where the person actually IS, in their own words: "Bole, Addis Ababa", "12 Biashara St, Kisumu".

country.description: …or an area we already serve, named exactly. `country` narrows either of the two above.

quoteId.description: A price held earlier. Give this OR the four fields below — never both.

buyerMobile.description: Somebody has to be told where to collect it.

contentPhotoRef.description: A photo of the contents — the baseline a damage claim is judged against. Upload it first.

externalOrderId.description: Your own order reference, carried through and returned on every callback.

items.description: What is in the box, and what it is worth. Required when the route crosses a border.
